original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Build reusable exact-search tooling (Python stdlib only) for noncommuting word/tuple enumeration over F2[G] group rings and M_r of them (GL_2(F2), Q8) with prefix closure bounds, memoized layer/signature digests, GL-conjugation symmetry reduction and parallel-safe batch splitting; demonstrate it on open problem KB2 (research/fiveswap-alt13-commuting-screen, PR 2317 open question 1): find or exclude the strictly alternating thirteen-call word at five fully occupied coordinate-SWAP roles in the formal F2[GL_2(F2)] rank-one-idempotent register model.
scope_change_reason: Authorized orchestrator tooling mandate: an explicit open request. The local draw (seed 56cf67ad450f0a4b6c78411360a6654f, track complex-mechanisms) proposed complex-new-helper-inventory / p104-side-correction / complex-rank-shape-decoder; the assigned open request supersedes the draw because the KB2 search was recorded as blocked on solver tooling (research/fiveswap-alt13-commuting-screen open question 1 names 'no SAT/SMT tooling on this host' as its blocker), and unblocking it is the deliverable. The mathematical object is unchanged from KB2; the method changes from analytic screening to exact solver tooling plus exhaustive noncommuting tuple search.
bottleneck_link: KB2 is the only remaining potential saving below the direct fifteen-call tariff at five fully occupied coordinate-SWAP roles in the fixed coordinate-CNOT alphabet (four-swap-full-occupancy uniform cut: q >= 2t+3 with equality strictly alternating, sign trace q = t mod 2 leaves only q = 13 for t = 5). Excluding it closes the alphabet at 3t; finding it would give the first saving in this model. The bit side does not bind and no kappa claim is made.
stop_rule: Stop the search when either (a) a thirteen-call word passes the exact formal endpoint check, or (b) the six-distinct-value family is completely excluded with receipts and the remaining seven-or-more-distinct frontier is recorded with exact covered/uncovered counts. Reserve the final session portion for controls, replay, overlap refresh and publication. One bounded pivot maximum.
evidence: Reusable stdlib tooling exact_search.py with 17 unit controls (tests/test_research_exact_word_search.py) plus verify.py's 10 control groups. Complete exact search of the six-distinct-value KB2 family: 323,963,640 placements (extra-position pattern x class assignment with odd multiplicities), 278,576 distinct canonical signatures, 700,496 exact M_5(F2[G]) product evaluations after a sound diagonal pre-filter, zero survivors; per-m signature digests in verify.py output and README. Positive-hit (planted target) and tiny t=2 completeness cross-checks show the search is neither vacuous nor lossy. Independent search-level audit agreeing with the concurrent analytic exclusion PR 2415 (released to Ross Richardson); d >= 7 distinct-value tuples remain uncovered.
author: Aaron Wang, with help from opencode
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance via opencode (agentic coding tool) in reasoning, implementation, verification and writing. Single agent; no independent human or proof-assistant review.

method.arithmetic: Exact F2 arithmetic only (bit-packed group algebra F2[G], matrices over it); no floating point in any acceptance path.
classification_lemmas: Sign equation plus natural-quotient block equations are equivalent to the full M_t(F2[G]) endpoint (F2[S_3] = F2[epsilon]/(epsilon^2) x M_2(F2) decomposition).
Any tuple with sum N_i = I_5 uses at least 5 distinct projector values; 5 rank-one idempotents summing to I_5 are automatically a dual frame (V^T U = I).
Hence any KB2 solution uses >= 6 distinct values; the 6-value case is exactly one dual frame (odd multiplicities) plus one extra projector of even multiplicity m_W in {2,4,6,8}.
method.enumeration: Gauge-fix the frame to the coordinate frame (GL_5 conjugation is an exact symmetry); enumerate the extra projector W over all 491 non-frame rank-one idempotents of M_5(F2), all placements of W positions and all class assignments with odd multiplicities; group placements by per-class segment-product signature (memoized digest) so each distinct signature x W pair is evaluated once, exactly, in M_5(F2[G]).
method.parameter_ranges: t = 5 registers; 13 positions; strictly alternating labels abab...a (the a<->b automorphism covers the mirror); paid alphabet = 496 binary rank-one idempotents u v^T (v^T u = 1) in M_5(F2) times labels g in {a,b}; target [s] I_5 with s = aba = bab.

initial_task: Reusable exact-search tooling for noncommuting word/tuple enumeration over F2[G] and M_r(F2[G]); demonstration on the KB2 strictly alternating thirteen-call five-SWAP candidate (find or exclude, else exact search frontier with controls).

open_questions.question: Do seven-or-more-distinct-value tuples need new machinery, or does a C-matrix DPLL with the idempotence equations as watched constraints close the remaining KB2 space at search level?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would give a search-level exclusion of all of KB2 independent of the PR 1989 bridge, and exercise the tooling on the unfactored tuple space.
open_questions.first_step: Branch on the gap-layer bits c_ij with C^2 = C as quadratic watched constraints and the four projected block equations as the leaf test; record node counts and pruning receipts.
open_questions.blocked_by: The high-degree Z polynomials need propagators; the 78 free bits are not enumerable directly.

open_questions.question: What are the exact weighted minima for the five-SWAP endpoint under asymmetric label prices (e.g. price(a)=1, price(b)=2)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR 2415's handoff lists changed charges as a remaining premise; asymmetric prices make longer a-heavy words competitive and the crossing rank no longer prices the minimum.
open_questions.first_step: Complete weighted minima for t = 2 and t = 3 with weighted layer digests; t = 2 is small enough for the current engine.
open_questions.blocked_by: Weighted search at t = 3 needs length-9 layers; the layer-ball engine is exponential in word length without the frame-family structure.

open_questions.question: Can a bit-sliced evaluator over candidate sets make m_W >= 6 and wider algebras cheap?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The u_c v_c masks already exist; bit-slicing would give roughly two orders of magnitude on candidate sweeps.
open_questions.first_step: Rewrite sig_eval's inner loop over 491-bit candidate masks; cross-check against the scalar evaluator on random tuples.
